To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the eye and the smile regions of emotional faces are lateralized (mainly right and left hemispheres, respectively) and are processed in parallel, (2) the smile region is visually salient, and (3) the smile region of happy faces is processed early (150-200 ms) and is used as a shortcut in expression identification.
the right hemisphere is involved in holistic processing, while the left hemisphere is involved in part-based processing of emotional facial expression.
holistic processing of emotional expressions is mainly lateralized in the right hemisphere, and analytic processing of the mouth region of the face occurs in the left hemisphere.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural mechanisms underlying the recognition of facial expressions, which is a fundamental aspect of social cognition and emotion processing.
the role of holistic versus analytical processing of facial expressions.
the neurocognitive processes involved in the holistic and part-based processing of emotional faces, which is relevant for understanding the mechanisms underlying social cognition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
holistic (mainly, right) and analytical (mainly, left) processing of facial expressions are dissociated, and occur in parallel.
the right hemisphere is involved in holistic processing of facial expressions, while the left hemisphere is specialized for analytical processing of the mouth region of a happy face.
the eye region is more important for anger than happiness, whereas the mouth region is more important in the case of happiness than anger.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

holistic and part-based processing are complementary, and that the former is dominant in the right hemisphere, while the latter is dominant in the left hemisphere, at least in the processing of facial emotions.

holistic processing is necessary to encode emotional expressions in the right hemisphere, while the mouth region of the smile is visually salient and is used for shortcut recognition in the left hemisphere.
the holistic processing of facial expressions is mainly right-lateralized, whereas the analytic processing of facial expressions, especially the happy face, is mainly left-lateralized.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the eye region of the angry face is not salient and is processed analytically later (450-600ms) than the mouth of the happy face.
the mouth of happy faces has a unique role in emotion recognition.

both holistic and part-based processing of emotional faces is lateralized, with the right hemisphere being dominant for holistic processing, while the left hemisphere is dominant for part-based processing.
